title: Time, days & months
goal: Tell the time, name the days and months, and talk about today, yesterday, tomorrow and next week.
intro: To ask the time in Odia you ask *how much has struck?* — **କେତେ ବାଜିଛି?** The hours take the classifier **-ଟା**, and there are special words for half past, quarter past and quarter to. Watch out for **କାଲି**: it means both *yesterday* and *tomorrow*; the verb tense tells you which.

vocab.note: Tense decides! To be explicit: ଗତକାଲି / ଆସନ୍ତାକାଲି.

phrases.en: I'll be there in five minutes.

grammar.title: Telling the time
grammar.body:
Ask **କେତେ ବାଜିଛି?** ('how much has struck?'). Answer with the hour + **-ଟା** + **ବାଜିଛି**: ଦଶଟା ବାଜିଛି 'it's ten o'clock'.

Fractions go *before* the hour:
**ସୱା** ଚାରିଟା — 4:15 (quarter past four)
**ସାଢ଼େ** ଚାରିଟା — 4:30 (half past four)
**ପାଉଣେ** ପାଞ୍ଚଟା — 4:45 (quarter to five)
Special: **ଡେଢ଼ଟା** 1:30, **ଅଢ଼େଇଟା** 2:30.

Other minutes: ଚାରିଟା ଦଶ '4:10'; ପାଞ୍ଚଟା ବାଜିବାକୁ ଦଶ ମିନିଟ୍ 'ten to five' (ten minutes until five strikes).

'At' a time: add **-ରେ** or **ବେଳେ**: ସାତଟାରେ / ସାତଟା ବେଳେ 'at seven'. Put the part of the day first: ସକାଳ ସାତଟା '7 a.m.', ରାତି ଦଶଟା '10 p.m.'.

examples.en: I get up at six in the morning.

grammar.title: Time expressions
grammar.body:
Time words usually come early in the sentence, often first. **କାଲି** is 'yesterday' with a past verb and 'tomorrow' with a future verb. Days: ସୋମବାର or ସୋମବାର ଦିନ 'on Monday'. 'Last' is **ଗତ** (ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହ 'last week'), 'next' is **ଆସନ୍ତା** (ଆସନ୍ତା ମାସ 'next month'). 'Per' uses **-କୁ**: ମାସକୁ 'per month', ଦିନକୁ ଦୁଇ ଥର 'twice a day'.

Useful endings: **-ରୁ** 'from' and **ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** 'until': ସୋମବାରରୁ ଶୁକ୍ରବାର ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ 'Monday to Friday'.

examples.en: The shop is closed on Mondays.
The Chariot Festival is next month.

examples.native: ମୁଁ ଦିନକୁ ଦୁଇ ଥର ଚା ପିଏ।
examples.roman: muṃ dinôku dui thôrô cha pie.
examples.en: I drink tea twice a day.

grammar.title: Months
grammar.body:
In daily life Odias use the English months, pronounced the Odia way:
ଜାନୁଆରୀ *januari* · ଫେବୃଆରୀ *phebruari* · ମାର୍ଚ୍ଚ *marchô* · ଅପ୍ରେଲ *ôprelô* · ମେ *me* · ଜୁନ *junô* · ଜୁଲାଇ *julai* · ଅଗଷ୍ଟ *ôgôsṭô* · ସେପ୍ଟେମ୍ବର *sepṭembôrô* · ଅକ୍ଟୋବର *ôkṭobôrô* · ନଭେମ୍ବର *nôbhembôrô* · ଡିସେମ୍ବର *ḍisembôrô*.

Festivals and farming follow the traditional calendar: ବୈଶାଖ, ଜ୍ୟେଷ୍ଠ, ଆଷାଢ଼, ଶ୍ରାବଣ, ଭାଦ୍ରବ, ଆଶ୍ୱିନ, କାର୍ତ୍ତିକ, ମାର୍ଗଶିର, ପୌଷ, ମାଘ, ଫାଲ୍ଗୁନ, ଚୈତ୍ର (roughly mid-April to mid-April). Dates: number + **ତାରିଖ**.

examples.en: Rath Yatra happens in the month of Asadha.

dialogue.title: Making plans for Sunday
dialogue.setting: Bapi phones Sam to arrange an outing.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.en: Tomorrow is Sunday. A day off.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ସକାଳେ ମୁଁ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ, କିନ୍ତୁ ସଞ୍ଜରେ ସମୟ ଅଛି।
lines.roman: sôkaḷe muṃ byôstô, kintu sôñjôre sômôyô ôchhi.
lines.en: I'm busy in the morning, but I'm free in the evening.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ଭଲ। ଚାଲ, ସଞ୍ଜ ପାଞ୍ଚଟା ବେଳେ ଏକାମ୍ର ହାଟ ଯିବା।
lines.roman: bhôlô. chalô, sôñjô pañchôṭa beḷe Ekamrô Haṭô jiba.
lines.en: Good. Let's go to Ekamra Haat at five in the evening.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.en: Five? Half past five would be better.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି, ସାଢ଼େ ପାଞ୍ଚଟା। ମୁଁ ତୁମ ଘରକୁ ଆସିବି।
lines.roman: ṭhik ôchhi, saṛhe pañchôṭa. muṃ tumô ghôrôku asibi.
lines.en: Okay, half past five. I'll come to your place.

lines.speaker: Bapi
lines.native: ନା ନା, ମୁଁ ଠିକ୍ ସମୟରେ ଆସିବି।
lines.roman: na na, muṃ ṭhik sômôyôre asibi.
lines.en: No, no, I'll come on time.

culture: Odisha's year is full of festivals tied to the traditional calendar: **ରଥଯାତ୍ରା** (Chariot Festival, in Asadha), **ରଜ** (a three-day festival in mid-June celebrating the earth and womanhood, with swings and *poṛô piṭha*), **ଦଶହରା/ଦୁର୍ଗା ପୂଜା** in autumn and **କାର୍ତ୍ତିକ ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣିମା** with *Boita Bandana*, when people float little boats to remember Odisha's ancient sea trade. 'Odia time' is relaxed — a 5 o'clock meeting may well start at half past.

tip.title: Telling the time
tip.body:
- Ask **କେତେ ବାଜିଛି?** 'how much has struck?'
- Answer: hour + **-ଟା** + ବାଜିଛି: ଦଶଟା ବାଜିଛି 'it's ten o'clock'. (Clock time always takes -ଟା, never -ଟି.)
- 'At' a time: **-ରେ** or **ବେଳେ**: ସାତଟାରେ / ସାତଟା ବେଳେ.
- 'In five minutes': ପାଞ୍ଚ ମିନିଟରେ.

sentences.en: What time is it now?
It's four o'clock.
It's nine o'clock — it's got late!
I'll come at seven.
Please come at two.
I'll be there in ten minutes.

sentences.native: ମୋ ପାଖରେ ଦୁଇ ଘଣ୍ଟା ସମୟ ଅଛି।
sentences.roman: mo pakhôre dui ghôṇṭa sômôyô ôchhi.
sentences.en: I have two hours free.
Do you have time?

tip.title: Quarter past, half past, quarter to
tip.body:
- Fractions go **before** the hour: **ସୱା** ଚାରିଟା 4:15 · **ସାଢ଼େ** ଚାରିଟା 4:30 · **ପାଉଣେ** ପାଞ୍ଚଟା 4:45. But 1:30 = **ଡେଢ଼ଟା**, 2:30 = **ଅଢ଼େଇଟା**.
- The part of the day comes first: **ସକାଳ** ସାତଟା 7 a.m. · **ସଞ୍ଜ** ଛଅଟା 6 p.m. · **ରାତି** ଦଶଟା 10 p.m.
- **-ରୁ** from · **ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** until.

sentences.en: It's half past seven.
Breakfast is at quarter past eight.
It's quarter to ten.
Come at half past one. (familiar)
The shop opens at ten in the morning.
Let's have tea at six this evening.
We eat at nine at night.

sentences.native: ଡାକ୍ତର ସକାଳ ନଅଟାରୁ ବାରଟା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ବସନ୍ତି।
sentences.roman: ḍaktôrô sôkaḷô nôṭaru barôṭa pôrjyôntô bôsônti.
sentences.en: The doctor sees patients from 9 a.m. until noon.
When does the shop close at night?

tip.title: Yesterday or tomorrow? କାଲି
tip.body:
- **କାଲି** means yesterday *and* tomorrow — the verb decides: କାଲି ମୁଁ **ଆସିଲି** 'I came yesterday', କାଲି ମୁଁ **ଆସିବି** 'I'll come tomorrow'.
- To be clear: **ଗତକାଲି** yesterday, **ଆସନ୍ତାକାଲି** tomorrow.
- Time words go near the start of the sentence.
- **କେବେ** when? · **ଏବେ** now.
tip.pattern: କାଲି + past = yesterday  ·  କାଲି + future = tomorrow

sentences.en: I'll come tomorrow.
Yesterday I ate a lot of fish.
I got back from Puri yesterday.
Tomorrow we'll go to Cuttack.
When will you come? (familiar)

sentences.native: ସେ ଏବେ ଘରେ ନାହାନ୍ତି, କାଲି ଆସନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: se ebe ghôre nahanti, kali asôntu.
sentences.en: He's not at home now — please come tomorrow.
I'm very busy today.
It's very hot in the daytime — come in the evening.

tip.title: Days of the week
tip.body:
- Every day ends in **-ବାର**: ସୋମବାର, ମଙ୍ଗଳବାର, ବୁଧବାର, ଗୁରୁବାର, ଶୁକ୍ରବାର, ଶନିବାର, ରବିବାର.
- 'On Monday': just ସୋମବାର, or ସୋମବାର **ଦିନ**.
- What day is it? **ଆଜି କି ବାର?**
- 'Monday to Friday': ସୋମବାର**ରୁ** ଶୁକ୍ରବାର **ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ**.

sentences.en: Today is Monday.
On Tuesday I'll go to Cuttack.
Are you free on Wednesday evening?

sentences.native: ଗୁରୁବାର ଦିନ ମୁଁ ମାଛ ଖାଏ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: gurubarô dinô muṃ machhô khae nahiṃ.
sentences.en: I don't eat fish on Thursdays.
Come to our place on Friday night. (familiar)
Saturday and Sunday are days off.
I'm busy from Monday to Friday.
See you on Sunday.

tip.title: Months and dates
tip.body:
- Everyday life uses the English months, said the Odia way: ଜାନୁଆରୀ, ଫେବୃଆରୀ, ମାର୍ଚ୍ଚ … ଡିସେମ୍ବର.
- Dates: number + **ତାରିଖ**: ଦଶ ତାରିଖ 'the 10th'. Asking: ଆଜି କେତେ ତାରିଖ?
- 'In May': ମେ **ମାସରେ**. **ଗତ** last, **ଆସନ୍ତା** next: ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହ, ଆସନ୍ତା ମାସ.
- 'A week': ସପ୍ତାହ**କୁ** ଦୁଇ ଥର 'twice a week'.

sentences.en: Today is the 15th.
When's your birthday?
My birthday is in May.
I'll come on 20 December.
Last week I went to Puri.
Next month I'll go to London.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ସପ୍ତାହକୁ ଦୁଇ ଥର ମାଛ ଖାଏ।
sentences.roman: muṃ sôptahôku dui thôrô machhô khae.
sentences.en: I eat fish twice a week.
When does Rath Yatra take place?
